guide.text:
# Pack context sections within a byte budget

> **In plain terms.** An assistant program can take in only so much text at once, so what it is given must be chosen to fit. This component is given ordered recipes listing sections of material, each with its text or a stated size, and a size limit. It goes down each list adding a section only if it fits in the space left, and skips any that do not. The result lists included and left-out sections with sizes but not text, so a reader can see what was dropped. One small decision step, whether a section fits, is checked by a mathematical proof against written rules.

This validator takes ordered context recipes and section material, measures available section bodies, falling back to a declared byte size when a body is unavailable, and includes each section if it fits the remaining byte budget. Its result lists included and omitted sections with sizes, while redacting their bodies. The token count is a rough estimate of one token per four bytes.

## Run the example

From the repository root, with Python 3.11 or newer and the checkout dependencies available:

```sh
PYTHONPATH=src python3 -m microcosm_core.organs.provider_context_recipe_budget_policy run-budget-bundle \
  --input examples/provider_context_recipe_budget_policy/exported_provider_context_budget_bundle \
  --out .microcosm/component-guides/provider_context_recipe_budget_policy
```

Inspect `.microcosm/component-guides/provider_context_recipe_budget_policy/exported_provider_context_budget_bundle_validation_result.json` for the result and findings.

The recipes fill sections in the declared order, skipping a section that does not fit. The omission list lets a reader see what was left out; it is not a transcript of material sent to a model.

## What the result means

Packs each ordered context recipe into its byte budget and lists included and omitted sections with sizes, rejecting a recipe that hides its omissions or permits proof bodies.

Related reading: [Retrieval-Augmented Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2005.11401), [Command Line Interface Guidelines](https://clig.dev/).

## Verification

The [Dafny-verified packing core](../formal/components/budget_packing/README.md) used by this projection includes each nonnegative-sized section exactly when it fits after earlier inclusions. It proves the included total stays within a nonnegative budget, including across batches. Python measures and normalizes the sizes and assembles the batches; those steps and any provider behavior remain outside the proof.

The direct command above calls the packing core. Separately, `make component-replays` applies the [shared admission check](../formal/replay/README.md) to observed replay identities and receipt agreement.

# Ordered budget packing

`BudgetPacking.dfy` verifies the ordered decision used by the provider-context
recipe projection. Given a sequence of nonnegative integer sizes and a signed
budget, `Pack` returns one decision for every input position, in order. A position
is included exactly when its size plus the total of earlier included positions
fits the budget. The returned total is the sum of included sizes; it does not
exceed a nonnegative budget. A negative budget includes nothing. The
`GreedyConcat` lemma proves that decisions from consecutive batches agree with
the same ordered rule when each batch receives the remaining budget.

The production hook is `_recipe_projection` in
`src/microcosm_core/organs/provider_context_recipe_budget_policy.py`. It computes
sizes using the existing text and declared-size rules, passes the normalized
integers through `plectis.components.budget_packing.pack`, and uses the returned
position decisions to assemble the original metadata. The wrapper batches long
sequences and calls the generated kernel through the shared isolated worker.
Inputs and the returned total use hexadecimal integers on the worker wire, so
Python's decimal JSON digit limit does not truncate the supported integer range.
Python normalization, UTF-8 byte counting, the adapter, batching and metadata
assembly, the worker and the Dafny compiler/runtime remain trusted. In particular,
a declared fallback size need not equal any actual body size. The shared worker has a timeout; it does not prove provider policy,
model behavior, or receipt authenticity.

The source-linked negative changes the fit test to compare each item against
the full budget instead of the remaining budget. The proof rejects that change;
for budget 10 and sizes 6, 6 it would include 12 bytes. `metadata.json` records
the source and generated hashes and the verification summaries. Reproduction
uses Dafny 4.11.0 and the repository's component-kernel checker; focused runtime
coverage is in `tests/test_component_budget_packing.py`.

excerpts.name: IncludedTotal
excerpts.text:
function IncludedTotal(sizes: seq<nat>, decisions: seq<bool>): nat
    requires |sizes| == |decisions|
    decreases |sizes|
  {
    if |sizes| == 0 then 0
    else (IncludedTotal(sizes[..|sizes|-1], decisions[..|decisions|-1]) +
          (if decisions[|decisions|-1] then sizes[|sizes|-1] else 0))
  }
